accuracy.evidence: Matches the England national curriculum English spoken-language and reading-aloud expectations (Year 2 read aloud with intonation, Years 3 to 6 perform and present with appropriate volume and intonation) and CCSS W.K.6 to W.5.6 on using digital tools to produce and publish writing with keyboarding. Yes/no questions rise at the end; the Plan, Draft, Edit, Publish, Share order follows the standard writing process.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the common errors: reading quietly so only the front row hears or shouting instead (volume dial and quiet/shout tags), rushing through full stops (pause step, rush tag), questions read flat or falling (contour prediction, downq and flat tags), pressing harder for a capital (Shift prediction), and publishing straight after planning (early and skip tags).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpublish pairs a volume dial with four rows of listeners who light up only when they can hear, tappable gaps after . ! and ?, three drawn intonation contours matched to sentences, an on-screen keyboard with Shift, Space, Backspace and full stop fixes, and a five-slot writing-process order. No other flag lab models audience reach or intonation; the shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The back row only lights up at level 4, so the link between volume and audience is seen, not told. Pauses are found by tapping the marks themselves, the contour drawing shows the voice rising on a question, and each key press visibly changes the typed sentence until it is correct, so pupils learn the fix by doing it.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions: who needs to hear you when you read to the class, whether your voice goes up or down at the end of 'Can I come too?', and how to type a capital letter. Each is answered by the dial, the contour and the keyboard step that follows.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with rotated answer order and ten tagged messages (quiet, shout, rush, end, downq, flat, space, dot, early, skip). Each explains the effect on the listener or reader, for example that rushing past a full stop runs two sentences together.

readability.evidence: Family audience: kid text FK 1.2 against the 5.0 target and adult text FK 7.8 against 10.0, as measured by the validator. Exact terms appear and are explained: intonation, volume, pause, full stop, question mark, Shift key, Backspace, draft, edit, publish.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean and overlap below 12 percent. Every kid paragraph carries a single practical skill (be heard, pause at the marks, let your voice show the punctuation, type it right, publish your best copy); adult paragraphs give curriculum references, named mistakes and the lab walkthrough.

mobile.evidence: Re-shot on iPhone 13 after the layout fix: pupils and the back-row label no longer overlap, the pause gaps have widened tap zones, the four keys sit in a 2 by 2 grid and the five process slots fit in one row. walk.cjs passes on desktop and iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: axe clean in light and dark. Volume has Quieter and Louder buttons, pauses have a Mark the next pause button, contours and keys are real buttons, and process cards can be tapped in order; a live region announces volume level, pauses found and the typed sentence.
